preamble: Stopping of the alveolar fricative [s] to [t]. The best-attested cases are coda neutralizations, in which a syllable-final sibilant surfaces as unreleased [t̚]. Examples are Thai loanwords from Indic (rasa > รส rót) and Korean native words (옷 /os/ > [ot̚]).

examples.note: Coda neutralization: a final sibilant surfaces as unreleased [t̚]; cf. Lao ລົດ
Coda /s/ neutralizes to unreleased [t̚]; [s] comes back before a vowel-initial suffix, as in 옷이 [osi].
